critique: The black background and white particle color are appropriate, but the render remains dramatically under-populated relative to a Brownian Motion fluid thumbnail. Frame 1 has only a handful of large isolated dots, and frame 4 has only a few dozen scattered blobs. This reads as a low-rate emitter accumulating particles rather than a dense field of fine particles already undergoing continuous fluid agitation. The visible particle-size setting also produces chunky specks instead of the preset's fine particulate texture.

suggestions.why: The active Gen1 emitter rate is still 20 particles/sec, which directly explains the sparse frame-to-frame buildup despite the separate visibility-floor rate setting. Raising the actual emitter rate establishes a substantially denser moving field immediately.

With the increased emission density, reducing maximum particle size from 6 to 2 changes the current conspicuous white blobs into the fine dust-like particles characteristic of the Brownian Motion thumbnail.
